answer: Metformin activates AMPK and inhibits mitochondrial complex I [s1]. Observational data in type 2 diabetics show lower all-cause mortality and lower cancer incidence in metformin users versus matched controls [s1]. The TAME trial (Targeting Aging with Metformin) is a proposed phase 3 trial of metformin against multimorbidity endpoints in older adults; it is not yet enrolling [s2]. The MILES study previously provided preliminary transcriptomic evidence of metformin's effect on aging-related pathways in older adults [s2]. Metformin is not FDA-approved for aging.

citations.title: Barzilai N et al. Metformin as a Tool to Target Aging. Cell Metab 2016
citations.snippet: Metformin activates AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), inhibits mitochondrial complex I, and has been associated with reduced all-cause mortality and reduced cancer incidence in observational studies of type 2 diabetics.

citations.title: TAME study rationale and design
citations.snippet: TAME (Targeting Aging with Metformin) is a proposed multicenter phase 3 trial of metformin against multimorbidity endpoints. The MILES (Metformin In Longevity Study) pilot provided preliminary transcriptomic data.

answer: Minoxidil was developed as an antihypertensive vasodilator (K-ATP channel opener); hair growth was observed as an off-target effect in patients receiving it for hypertension [s1]. Topical minoxidil requires sulfation by scalp SULT1A1 to its active metabolite minoxidil sulfate, and SULT1A1 activity predicts response to topical minoxidil [s1].

citations.title: Goren A et al. SULT1A1 activity and topical minoxidil response. Skin Appendage Disord 2018
citations.snippet: Minoxidil was originally developed as an antihypertensive vasodilator acting on potassium ATP channels; hypertrichosis was observed as an off-target effect. Topical minoxidil requires sulfation by SULT1A1 in the scalp to its active form, minoxidil sulfate. SULT1A1 activity in plucked hair follicles predicts response.

answer: Thalidomide and its analogs lenalidomide and pomalidomide bind cereblon (CRBN), the substrate adapter of the CRL4 E3 ubiquitin ligase, which redirects the ligase to neomorphic substrates IKZF1 and IKZF3 [s1]. Degradation of IKZF1/3 underlies the anti-myeloma activity of these IMiDs [s1]. The same cereblon-mediated mechanism also explains thalidomide's teratogenicity via degradation of SALL4, identified more recently [s2].

citations.title: Lu G et al. The Myeloma Drug Lenalidomide Promotes the Cereblon-Dependent Destruction of IKZF1 and IKZF3. Science 2014
citations.snippet: Lenalidomide acts through cereblon (CRBN), the substrate adapter of the CRL4 E3 ubiquitin ligase, to selectively destabilize the transcription factors IKZF1 and IKZF3, which are required for myeloma cell survival. Thalidomide and pomalidomide share this mechanism.

citations.title: Donovan KA et al. Thalidomide promotes degradation of SALL4. eLife 2018
citations.snippet: Thalidomide binding to cereblon induces ubiquitination and degradation of the transcription factor SALL4. SALL4 loss-of-function causes a developmental phenotype that recapitulates thalidomide teratogenicity.

answer: Nirmatrelvir inhibits the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro / 3CLpro) [s1]. The scaffold was derived from earlier Pfizer programs against SARS-CoV-1 protease (e.g. PF-00835231) and was optimized for oral bioavailability [s1]. Mpro cleaves the viral polyproteins pp1a and pp1ab to release the non-structural proteins essential for replication [s1]. Because nirmatrelvir is metabolized by CYP3A4 to a less-active form, it is co-administered with ritonavir as a pharmacokinetic booster [s1]. In EPIC-HR, nirmatrelvir/ritonavir reduced the composite of hospitalization or death by ~89% in high-risk unvaccinated adults treated within 3 days of symptom onset [s2].

citations.title: Owen DR et al. An oral SARS-CoV-2 Mpro inhibitor clinical candidate (nirmatrelvir). Science 2021
citations.snippet: Nirmatrelvir (PF-07321332) was developed from earlier intravenous SARS-CoV-1 protease inhibitors (notably PF-00835231) by introducing oral-bioavailability-conferring features. It is a covalent inhibitor of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro, which cleaves polyproteins pp1a/pp1ab; metabolism is dominated by CYP3A4, motivating co-administration with ritonavir as a pharmacokinetic enhancer.

citations.title: Hammond J et al. Oral Nirmatrelvir for High-Risk, Nonhospitalized Adults with Covid-19 (EPIC-HR). NEJM 2022
citations.snippet: In high-risk, unvaccinated, symptomatic adults with COVID-19, nirmatrelvir plus ritonavir initiated within 3 days of symptom onset reduced the composite of hospitalization or death by 89.1% compared with placebo.
